_description: Conformance vectors for traigent_schema/best_config_profile.py, the best-config hash profile layered on top of fp2 (fp2's own corpus is tests/data/fp2_conformance.json and is untouched by this file). These vectors are value-level, not lexical: JSON has one number literal grammar, and this file's 'unsafe_integral_int' vs 'unsafe_integral_float' distinction survives ONLY because Python's json module happens to parse a JSON number without '.' or 'e'/'E' as int and one with either as float. A JS JSON.parse would collapse both into the same Number and cannot reproduce this int/float split - so these vectors describe what the PARSED PYTHON VALUE must do, not a claim that raw JSON text carries a portable int/float distinction. Canonical-byte-length boundary vectors (exactly MAX_CANONICAL_SPEC_BYTES / +1 / astral-character byte counting) are deliberately NOT stored here: a 256KiB literal fixture would bloat the repo for no benefit, so tests/test_best_config_profile.py generates those cases programmatically against best_config_profile.MAX_CANONICAL_SPEC_BYTES instead.

safe_integer_boundary.description: abs(n) == 2**53-1 is the largest integral magnitude fp2 and the profile both still accept.

unsafe_integral_int.description: A Python int exceeding the safe range. Rejected by fp2 itself AND by the profile's prevalidation.

unsafe_integral_float.description: The same magnitude as unsafe_integral_int, expressed with a JSON literal that parses to a Python float. fp2 canonicalizes this on its own (it is an ordinary finite float to fp2) - only the profile's prevalidation rejects it, which is the entire reason this profile exists.

nested_unsafe_integral.description: The unsafe float is three containers deep; prevalidation must walk the full structure, not just top-level values.
